W001-deterministic.md Card B lost its proposed speedup because the giant points remained arbitrary for a generic multipoint tree. H012 explored reciprocal certificate reuse and found finite valid covers; first independent review now proposes an Ω(phi(m)*n) full-range, per-residue representation obstruction, separately under independent review. Read W001 Card A, Card B and shared costs, H012-certificate-reuse.md, H012-independent-review.md, research/hypotheses/H015.md, H015-geometric-family-bound.md, and H015-short-block-extension.md in FULL. H015 is parent mathematics, no experiments or Lean theorem. Its motivation is actual geometric structure: for fixed (u,t,r=v mod m²), giant exponents E=u+v+Nt give alpha^E = alpha^(u+r+Nt)*gamma^k, gamma=alpha^(m²), v=r+m²*k. Gaps in k are not free.

First parent claim: suppose N,m>0, gcd(N,m)=1, H<=C sqrt(Nm), fixed C, and every unit residue j has an informative integer certificate covering one entire cell [P,2P], sqrt(N)/4<=P<=sqrt(N)/2. Its congruences are v+2uj=0 mod m and Nt+uj²+vj=0 mod m². Three evaluations at P,3P/2,2P give |u|<=12H/P and |t|<=24HP/N, hence |u|<=48C sqrt(m), |t|<=12C sqrt(m). At large m, u=0 or t=0 contradict informativeness and u*j²=Nt mod m. A fixed (u,t,v mod m²) family serves at most gcd(2u,m)<=96C sqrt(m) residues, so at least phi(m)/(96C sqrt(m)) families. This does NOT count all possible merging of different families.

Stronger new extension to inspect carefully:
Fix nonzero t, g=gcd(t,m). Every valid u has gcd(u,m)=g. There are at most 2U/g choices of nonzero u with |u|<=U=48C sqrt(m). For each, dividing congruence by g gives a unit quadratic-root congruence modulo m/g. It has at most R_m=2^(omega(m)+1) roots, each with at most g lifts to residues modulo m. Thus each t serves <=2U R_m residues and at least D=phi(m)/(96C sqrt(m) R_m)=m^(1/2-o(1)) distinct t are needed. This includes nonprimitive u,t and arbitrary smooth m, no distribution of square residues assumed.
Same-cell bounds give |v|<=37H and |u|<=12H if P>=1, so E lies in [Nt-49H,Nt+49H]. If H<=N/196, bands for different t are separated by >=N/2. A literal integer-exponent run b,b+m²,...,b+(L-1)m² meeting two bands needs L>=1+N/(2m²). Therefore below that total represented-run-length budget, at least D separate runs are required, even when different u,v families merge. At m=N^(1/5+o(1)), this means exponentially many short runs (N^(1/10-o(1))) or at least N^(3/5-o(1)) padded positions to bridge one gap. This is NOT a bit-runtime lower bound for unimplemented compressed products. Modular order identifications, other strides, sparse exponent evaluators, or avoiding full whole-cell coverage are outside the theorem.

Independently accept/revise/reject both derivations with exact constants, quantifiers, rounding boundaries and capacity counts. Pay attention to unit square roots modulo prime powers, gcd division, negative t/v, distinctness of t versus modular giant values, actual exponents versus exponents reduced by an order, and the difference between number of families and occupied contiguous blocks. The parent explicitly did not prove that every batching algorithm is slow. Check use of Bostan–Schost (field operations) as background only; no field assumption can be imported over Z/NZ. No general product-tree lower bound follows from a conventional O(M(G) log L) upper formula.

Deliver a concise but self-contained critical review, fixes if any, and the precise surviving escape condition. A new algorithm or large survey is not requested. If a finite check is necessary, preregister it and a <=60-second cap first, retain every outcome and hashes; otherwise proof review alone suffices. No novelty claim or new factoring complexity bound. Keep the separate H012 obstruction and H014 changed-resultant enumerator tasks independent.
